subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB678 (2026-09-05): the TWO sequences GR5 determines separately are now resolved as a pair (SortCollation) and selected per key by the key's CLASS through the one classifier CollatingSelection.Of - alphabet-name-1 (GR5a) or the alphanumeric program collating sequence (GR5b) for keys of class alphabetic and alphanumeric, alphabet-name-2 (GR5a) or the national program collating sequence (GR5b) for keys of class national, and NO sequence for the two classes GR5 names neither of (numeric, boolean). Both formats take the same selection: the Format-1 file sort carries the class on its runtime key descriptor (CobolSort.KeyClass) and the Format-2 table sort chooses the comparer's carrier argument. Before this the statement carried ONE sequence, the alphanumeric weights were applied to a national key's UTF-16BE record bytes, and the table-sort form staged loud on recognition. Below 2002 the national half is unreachable (alphabet-name-2 and the FOR forms draw COBOL0872 - the negative case), so the alphanumeric half is what conforms at 85. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/CobolSort.cs#SequenceFor (kb/Work PB3339 moved the GR5 class-to-sequence selection, unchanged, out of CobolSort into SortKeyColumns)
